condition: Pre-operative assessment — drug-eluting stent 3 months after NSTEMI (elective surgery)
permutationLabel: DES 3 months after NSTEMI on aspirin + ticagrelor
summary: 61-year-old man on aspirin and ticagrelor 3 months after NSTEMI treated with a drug-eluting stent, referred for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for recurrent biliary colic.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative assessment for planned gallbladder operation
inputs.hpi: Four attacks of right upper quadrant colic in 6 months, none in the last 5 weeks, no jaundice or cholecystitis. NSTEMI 3 months ago treated with a drug-eluting stent to the circumflex artery; on aspirin and ticagrelor since. No angina since the stent. Asking to have the gallbladder removed as soon as possible.

exam.general: Well. HR 64, BP 128/80, RR 14, SpO2 98% on air, T 36.6°C.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple mobile gallstones, gallbladder wall 2 mm, no pericholecystic fluid. CBD 4 mm. Liver normal.

surgicalHistory: PCI with drug-eluting stent (circumflex) 3 months ago

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Pre-operative assessment — symptomatic gallstones; DES 3 months after NSTEMI on dual antiplatelet therapy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic cholelithiasis, currently quiescent. Drug-eluting stent 3 months after NSTEMI on aspirin + ticagrelor. Elective, not time-sensitive surgery.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Triage emergency_now: 'Possible biliary obstruction' (urgent) fires on the negated 'no jaundice' in the HPI.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: adaptiveTriage is a front-desk intake engine: its keyword red flags ('bleeding', 'breathless', 'collapse', 'jaundice', 'drain', 'procedure') fire on negated or historical mentions in a clinician's pre-operative note. Use negation handling and do not derive the consultation's emergency level from free-text keyword hits alone in a scheduled pre-operative/endoscopy encounter.

mustInclude.note: ESC 2022: delay elective non-cardiac surgery until 12 months after ACS (6 months after elective PCI); quiescent biliary colic is not time-sensitive.
Any interruption of P2Y12 inhibition early after a stent is a joint decision with the cardiologist (stent thrombosis risk).

mustExclude.note: Stopping the P2Y12 inhibitor 3 months after ACS without cardiology input risks stent thrombosis.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: 2022 ESC guidelines — cardiovascular assessment and management of patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery (with ESAIC)
guideline.section: Clinical risk (RCRI), functional capacity (e.g. climbing two flights of stairs); ECG and NT-proBNP/BNP and troponin in patients with risk factors before intermediate/high-risk surgery; echocardiography in poor functional capacity, raised NT-proBNP or known HF; delay elective surgery until 6 months after elective PCI and 12 months after ACS; continue aspirin after PCI if bleeding risk allows; interrupt P2Y12 inhibitors only in agreement with the cardiologist; bridging not recommended for antiplatelet interruption
guideline.citation: Halvorsen S, Mehilli J, Cassese S, et al. 2022 ESC Guidelines on cardiovascular assessment and management of patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Eur Heart J. 2022;43:3826–924.

guideline.name: ACCP guideline — perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy
guideline.section: VKA: stop 5 days before surgery; in AF suggest against heparin bridging; suggest bridging for mechanical mitral valve; DOAC: interrupt 1 day before low/moderate bleed-risk and 2 days before high bleed-risk procedures, no heparin bridging, no pre-operative coagulation testing; aspirin: continue in patients with coronary stents; P2Y12 inhibitors: stop clopidogrel/ticagrelor 5 days and prasugrel 7 days before surgery; defer elective surgery after recent stent
guideline.citation: Douketis JD, Spyropoulos AC, Murad MH, et al. Perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy: an American College of Chest Physicians clinical practice guideline. Chest. 2022;162:e207–43.

rationale: Permutation: recent coronary stent on DAPT. The index safety action is to defer elective surgery (12 months after ACS), keep aspirin, and involve cardiology before any P2Y12 interruption.
